summary: Allocate-and-copy helper for C strings: if the input `this` is non-null, allocates strlen(this)+1 bytes through MallocWrapperForNhMalloc (0x0058A935) and strcpy's the source into the fresh buffer; returns the new buffer or NULL when the input was null or the allocation failed. Called by SingletonGlobalAccessorWithFallbackAlloc (0x00564270) and sub_563870 (0x00563870), which then own the returned buffer.

operations.description: Initialize the result pointer to NULL before the input check.
Guard: only proceed when the input string `this` is non-null; otherwise return NULL.
Guard: if the allocation returned NULL, leave result NULL and return it (no copy).
Copy the source string into the fresh buffer with strcpy (compiler intrinsic, so no separate callee entry).
Return the allocated and copied buffer, or NULL when input was null or allocation failed.
Callers: sub_563870 (0x00563870) and SingletonGlobalAccessorWithFallbackAlloc (0x00564270) use this to obtain owned string copies.

unresolved: Ownership semantics: the returned buffer is transferred to the caller; the packet gives no free-site evidence.
strlen and strcpy are compiler intrinsics and therefore have no packet callee entries; only their effect is represented.
